summary.en: NTUTEC (台大創創中心), operating since 2013, is National Taiwan University's flagship entrepreneurship hub. Over 13 years it has mentored 600+ startup teams through an equity-free pipeline: NTU Garage (idea-to-MVP, ~20 teams/year, March–December), the NTU Accelerator (pre-A/Series A startups <7 years old), a Corporate Vertical Accelerator (35 corporate partners, 27 batches), and the NTUTEC Angels Club (150+ investor network). Notable alumni include BotBonnie (acquired by Appier), MoBagel, Vocus and 3drens.

summary.en: IAPS (陽明交大產業加速器), founded in 2013 at National Chiao Tung University (now NYCU) in Hsinchu, was the first university-affiliated startup accelerator established by academia in Taiwan. It has worked with 950+ startups and lab teams, with annual cumulative fundraising exceeding NT$300M (~US$10–11M per cohort). In 2015 it was ranked the top accelerator in the Asia-Pacific region and 7th globally by UBI Global. Programs include TTA, SPIN, iCAN and TX Venture, plus an Access-to-Taiwan (A2T) landing program for international startups.

summary.en: The TMU BioMed Accelerator (北醫生醫加速器), established by Taipei Medical University in 2018, is Taiwan's first international-class medical-university accelerator. It focuses on biomedical startups across digital health, AI and medical devices, running two cohorts a year and leveraging its 1-university/6–7-hospital clinical system (4,000+ beds, 7,000+ medical professionals). It has accelerated 100+ domestic and international startups and invested in around 8, co-investing with partner Wing Capital (比翼資本) — including US$100,000 each into three more mature teams. Teams have come from France, Singapore, Taiwan, Japan and Canada.
